item.title: The space superiority imperative to increase ground and network resilience
item.description: The past three decades have seen a marked increase in the capability, capacity and integration of American space capabilities to enhance and conduct combat operations. That same period has seen a corresponding growth in the threats against those space systems. Many have been focused on the increasingly capable spectrum of threats posed by China, including cyber, direct-ascent and co-orbital systems, or the spread of GPS and SATCOM jammers to countries around the world. However, a more rudimentary threat has also emerged: attacks against the ground stations that connect end users to space data and services. These ground systems are now in the crosshairs as a lucrative target for adversaries that do not possess the means or will to attack satellites.

item.title: Musk blames India’s oligarchs, New Delhi cites security and the villages keep waiting
item.description: Late on October 7, Elon Musk complained on X that “certain oligarchs” were keeping Starlink out of India, and the next day he asked, by name , whether Mukesh Ambani really runs the country. India’s communications ministry answered that all three licensed satellite operators sit at the same stage of review, that security checks are still under way for all of them, and it called the charge “baseless and misconceived.”
